The 16 favourites were originally priced at $150–$180; seven remain available from the Drunk Beaver Rocks Webstore. The ranking leads with Olbia Super-Klone, (Boba) FET OverBooster, Trainer TS-15 MKII, Inglorious Bastard V3 and Bloom V2, followed by Khelnytskyi OD, Kyiv Lead, Mykolaiv, Forest Song, Kavun, Vatra, Mariupol, Hostomel, Lutsk, Kherson and Okhtyrka. Across them are evolved Klon, FET, Traynor, Blues Breaker, Expandora, OD-1, SD-2, Magnetic Saturation, Screamer, MOSFET, Jazz Chorus, Tube Driver, Tweed 5E3, SD-1 and Honey Bee designs. In the wake of the quite superb recent Olbia Super-Klone - which is my favourite Drunk Beaver Overdrive to-date as well as by far and away my favourite evolved Klon sound. I thought I should do a roundup / overview of my other favourite Drunk Beaver Overdrives too. This listing and visual is roughly in order of my preferences - where fortunately - the first 5 pedals listed are mostly on general release. Vitalii has made 26 Overdrives so far by my count. Actually there’s a couple of earlier editions that I missed out on - the T-Rex Custom Tube Bender with Mod, and the Alpaca Drive take on the Red Llama. Vitalii is considering re-issuing those at some stage - so I might end up at full completion in the end! All of Vitalii’s takes are enhanced and evolved from the original source material - sometimes significantly so. While even the simplest of these has some highly unique aspects for their overall makeup and output texture! So 17 of the 26 were pedal drops, with the remainder being Mainstream / General Release editions - I ended up somewhat serendipitously with half-and-half General Releases and Pedal Drops in my rundown of 16. I thought it best to draw a line somewhere - while I could have included a few more - there’s only a tiny number of Drunk Beaver Overdrives that I didn’t gel with ... yet! As mentioned - these are listed largely in order of preference - while the later selections become a little more nebulous on relative positions. - **Identity basis:** Contemporary exact-model coverage identifies the Kavun MOS Drive as a Denys Toporchuk signature Drunk Beaver MOSFET overdrive with a five-control interface.

The **Drunk Beaver Kavun MOSFET Drive** is a MOSFET-based overdrive with a dedicated three-band EQ and separate Level and Drive controls. Contemporary coverage identifies the control set as **Bass, Mid, Treble, Level, and Drive**. [1]

The product is associated with **Denys Toporchuk** as a signature model. The archive preserves that signature relationship as part of the model context without treating it as a sonic or technical claim. [1]

- **Bass:** controls the low-frequency portion of the signal.
- **Mid:** controls the midrange.
- **Treble:** controls the high-frequency portion.
- **Level:** overall output.
- **Drive:** amount of overdrive/gain. [1]

The three-band EQ is a defining part of the interface. Contemporary coverage describes the pedal as a particularly shapeable MOSFET overdrive, but those are reviewer/player observations rather than laboratory measurements. [1]

The product name and contemporary coverage support the **MOSFET** circuit characterization. The reviewed sources do not expose a complete factory schematic, exact transistor part numbers, clipping-diode inventory, or universal production BOM.

The archive therefore records MOSFET architecture only at the level supported by the model name and exact-model coverage.

The Kavun appears in contemporary Drunk Beaver coverage among the brand's newer overdrive releases and as a signature model. The reviewed source does not establish a complete first-release date, production run, or revision chronology. [1][2]
